title: The stolen blessing (Genesis 27)
hookLine: Jacob in goatskins deceives his blind father, and Esau weeps
last: NOT FOR A BOWL OF STEW.

lines: NOT HOW YOU'D WRITE YOUR HEROES.
A BLIND FATHER, AND A LIE.
cards: If you were inventing a holy book to make your people look good, you would not write this chapter.

The man the whole nation will be named after, the grandson of Abraham, puts on his brother's clothes, ties goatskins to his arms so he'll feel hairy, carries in a dish his mother cooked, and lies to his blind, aging father's face, more than once.
And it works. Genesis tells it in slow, painful detail, as if it wants you to sit in the room. Isaac is old, his eyes have failed, and he wants to bless his favorite son before he dies.

teach.h: A MOTHER'S PLAN, TWO YOUNG GOATS.
teach.b: First, the plan. Isaac sends Esau out to hunt game and make the savory meat he loves, so he can bless him. Rebecca overhears.
She has Jacob bring two young goats, cooks them the way Isaac likes, dresses Jacob in Esau's best clothes, and covers his hands and neck with the skins.
Jacob worries about being caught, and she says, upon me be thy curse, my son. Second, the scene. Isaac is suspicious.
You came back so fast? Come close, let me feel you.

teach.h: THE VOICE OF JACOB, THE HANDS OF ESAU.
teach.b: Then the well-known line, in the Douay-Rheims: "The voice indeed is the voice of Jacob; but the hands are the hands of Esau." He asks straight out, are you my son Esau? And Jacob says, I am.
Isaac smells the field on his clothes, and blesses him with dew of heaven and fatness of the earth. Third, the other door. Jacob has barely left when Esau comes in with his dish.
Who are you? Your firstborn, Esau. And Isaac trembles.
Esau roars out with a great cry: "Bless me also, my father." Have you only one blessing, father? And he weeps, a grown man, a hunter.
Fourth, what the Bible does with it. It doesn't hide it. Augustine read the trick as a mystery pointing beyond itself.

teach.h: THE PROMISE GOES THROUGH A BROKEN HOME.
teach.b: Other readers simply let it stand: God's promise goes on through a family that lies, plays favorites and breaks.
Esau says in his heart he'll kill his brother. Rebecca sends Jacob away for a few days, she says. Genesis never records her seeing him again.

how: Catholics examine their consciences before confession, and the Church teaches that lying offends against truth and that repairing harm done by a lie is part of making amends.

a disguise of goatskins and borrowed clothes
a blessing, spoken by a father to his son

games.q: you're Isaac, old and blind. the man before you has Esau's hairy hands and smells of the field, but the voice is wrong. what do you do?
o: refuse to bless him until you're sure.
games.why: "The voice indeed is the voice of Jacob; but the hands are the hands of Esau." he asks, he doubts, and he blesses him anyway.

practice: Let your memory go back, gently, to a time you let someone believe something that wasn't true: a version of events that made you look better, a credit you didn't correct.
Don't punish yourself; just look at it the way Genesis does, plainly, and ask what one honest step would look like now. If you pray, bring it to God first.

wordCard.voice: Berakhah, blessing, in Hebrew: what Jacob stole from his blind father in his brother's clothes, while Esau wept too late. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: blessing. yesterday Jacob took the bekhorah, the birthright; today the berakhah.

carryVoice: Your line: the bible doesn't hide it. Its heroes come with their flaws showing. That's day three hundred fifty-five.
